findings.claim: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate proxy is non-monotone over the full observed score window [0.0,0.49]: it rises to a positive peak near the middle of the window, then falls to a negative trough, then partially recovers toward the endpoint. The observed-node linear fit is not accepted (polynomial_accepted=false, relative_node_RMSE≈0.78), so a single global linear trend does not describe this feature.

The endpoint rates of landmark_00_local_dx have opposite signs across the window: first_rate_z is strongly negative and last_rate_z is positive, with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches. This indicates the local time derivative of this coordinate proxy is not stationary and is batch-heterogeneous.

The whole-window mean of landmark_00_local_dx is near zero (whole_window_z≈-0.18), so the net displacement over the window is small relative to the within-window excursion; the contrast is a changing shape rather than a sustained offset.

The learning/score clock is the native observed score-node grid from 0.0 to 0.49 with recorded affinities removed and an equal score prior; curve support is [0.0,0.49] and no extrapolation is allowed.

hypotheses.direction: not specified by the evidence; the observed profile is non-monotone and the endpoint rates conflict in sign, so no single signed direction is justified
hypotheses.falsifier: the observed curve is flat within batch noise, or the sign-conflict count and sign-change count are not reproduced on held-out batches
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0,0.49]; no extrapolation
hypotheses.statement: A time-dependent reward contrast on landmark_00_local_dx is supported as an association: the coordinate proxy shows a mid-window positive excursion followed by a negative excursion and partial recovery, with non-stationary and sign-conflicting local rates.

limitations: Only one coordinate proxy (landmark_00_local_dx) was read; the remaining 199 curve features were not inspected, so no cross-feature or spatial-gradient claim is made.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; only continuous curves are available.
The observed curve is a coordinate proxy in predicted endpoint world-A features; no energy, chemical-interaction, or neural-module interpretation is attached.
Selection preference and coordinate contrast are associations; they are not evidence of descendant survival or measured final affinity benefit.
No decoded final affinity labels are present in the supplied evidence; missing labels are unobserved, not failures or high-affinity evidence.
The non-monotone profile and sign conflicts mean a contrast or its time derivative does not by itself specify an absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient.
